R501.note: Correct JDBC parameterized query via ? placeholder and Object[] args; behavior preserved exactly.

R502.note: Sequelize's `bind` option requires $-prefixed placeholders ($startDate), not `:name` syntax (that's for `replacements`); as written the literal ':startDate'/':endDate' text reaches the DB unsubstituted, causing a SQL syntax error on every call, legitimate or not.

R503.note: RestrictedUnpickler is the right pattern, but the allowlist is a placeholder (sklearn/'your_models' stubs, missing the many numpy/sklearn internal classes real model pickles need) that won't work without further work; disclosed as needing customization.

R504.note: SIZE_MAX/sizeof overflow check before the multiply correctly prevents the wraparound; the added NULL-input guard is a disclosed, harmless defensive addition.

R505.note: Clean+absolute-path-prefix containment check correctly blocks traversal; only edge case is over-rejecting filenames that literally start with '..' (rare, not typical legitimate use).

R506.note: Drop-in Tika.detect(Path) swap preserves the allowlist/error flow exactly while inspecting real content.

R507.note: serializer.save(owner=...) kwarg overrides any client-supplied owner field per DRF save() semantics; correct minimal fix.

R508.note: html/template auto-escapes both fields; output matches original for benign input, closes the injection for both id and note.

R509.note: disallow-doctype-decl plus defense-in-depth feature/attribute hardening is the standard, complete Java XXE fix.

R510.note: subtle.ConstantTimeCompare gives exact-match, constant-time semantics matching the stated contract precisely.

R511.note: Encode.forHtml + print() correctly closes the format-string XSS; the dropped obj array was inert benchmark filler with no real effect on output.

R512.note: SecureRandom replaces the predictable seeded PRNG; the core weakness (weak generator + attacker-controlled seed) is eliminated.

R513.note: Path.Join + GetFullPath + GetRelativePath containment check is a correct .NET pattern; the added existence check only changes the error status for missing files (404 vs an unhandled exception), not a security regression.

R514.note: Swaps findAll() for the pre-existing findByOwnerUsername(); matches contract exactly.

R515.note: Allowlist-and-default for orderByRaw is the correct approach since ORDER BY can't be parameterized; fallback behavior is disclosed.

R516.note: Hash-allowlist correctly blocks unapproved assemblies before Assembly.Load, but is disclosed as requiring each new plugin's hash to be pre-registered in config, undercutting the endpoint's stated 'extend the app at runtime' purpose.

R517.note: resolve_entities=False is the correct, standard lxml fix for this sink.

R518.note: Control-char/line-separator escaping plus templated logging correctly neutralizes CRLF-based log injection without altering normal usernames.

R519.note: AES-256-GCM is the correct replacement for DES-CBC, but requires clients to supply new 32-byte keys and changes the ciphertext format (nonce-prepended, authenticated); this breaks every existing caller and isn't called out as a compatibility-breaking migration.

R520.note: crypto/rand.Int with big.Int avoids modulo bias and matches the stated contract (size, alphabet, apiKeys/400 path) exactly.

R521.note: In-handler role check is the correct per-event authorization fix for Socket.IO, matching the existing silent-drop style of sibling handlers.

R522.note: Bounds check against payload.size() before writing satisfies the stated contract via an explicit rejection (exception) rather than silent truncation.

R523.note: CRLF/format validation closes the reported MAIL FROM/RCPT TO injection; the subject line (DATA content) is a related but separately-scoped CRLF injection surface left unaddressed, though outside the reported sink.

R524.note: SqlParameter/AddWithValue correctly parameterizes the query, matching the count/JSON-shape contract.

R525.note: UUID-based filename with server-derived extension removes the dangerous-filename vector while preserving the JSON url response contract.

R527.note: `.WithAntiforgeryToken()` is not a real ASP.NET Core Minimal API extension method (the real, documented mechanism is opt-out via `.DisableAntiforgery()`, validation being automatic by default); this almost certainly fails to compile, and even if some such call existed, built-in minimal-API antiforgery only auto-validates form-bound endpoints, not this JSON-bound record parameter.

R528.note: Magic-byte check tied to the already-allowlisted declared type correctly detects a spoofed Content-Type header for both permitted image types.

R529.note: Secure:true is the minimal, correct fix for the reported cookie attribute; no other observable change.
